content:
Facts: Pretermitted daughter sued siblings for reduction of mother's public will appointing brother sole heir; mother's will acknowledged having purchased two properties (one for each daughter) entirely with her money, declaring daughters satisfied; plaintiff contested indirect donations in siblings' favor (brother's two properties purchased with mother's funds); defendants contested indirect donation to plaintiff (her property purchased with mother's money per extrajudicial declaration) and alleged additional donations (car purchase, cash gifts to sister, sister's rent-free apartment use).
Legal Framework: Articles 537, 556, 724, 737, 746-747, 750 Italian Civil Code (legitimate portions with multiple children; fictitious reunion; collation obligations; donation valuation at succession opening); Arts. 2697, 2712, 2729, 2735 (burden of proof; mechanical reproduction; presumptions; extrajudicial confession).
Interpretive Issues: Evidentiary value of testator's public will declaration that legitimate heirs already satisfied through indirect donations; burden of proof allocation for alleged indirect donations requiring collation; qualification as indirect donation requiring animus donandi and teleological link between money provision and property purchase; admissibility timing for collation claims regarding donations mentioned only in post-resumption pleadings; probative sufficiency of extrajudicial declarations acknowledging donation receipt; treatment of joint bank account balances when pension/rent deposited but also unexplained transfers occurred; scope of estate debts deductible from relictum.
Principles Applied: Testator's public will declaration of prior satisfaction through donations lacks confessional value (fact contrary to third-party legitimate heir, not declarant) but constitutes evidence combinable with other serious, precise, consistent elements rising to full proof per Art. 2729. Declaration cannot deprive legitimate heir of reserved share via false statement but gains substantive/probative relevance preventing attribution of additional assets exceeding intended legitimate portion. Extrajudicial defendant declaration (contemporaneous with property purchase deed) acknowledging donation receipt, specifying payment methods, undertaking collation obligation constitutes confession per Arts. 2735, 2712; fully effective absent signature/content contestation. Generic late contestation of animus donandi without supporting evidence insufficient when contradicts defendant's own contractual declaration corroborated by testamentary disposition. Teleological link between money provision and property purchase establishes property (not money) as indirect donation object for collation per Arts. 724, 746. Party alleging indirect donation bears full proof burden; mere transfer allegation without demonstrating payment occurrence inadequate. Joint account balance presumptively co-owned; rebutting requires relevant presumptive evidence proving exclusive ownership; unexplained incoming transfers benefiting single account holder negate exclusive deceased ownership claim. Collation claims regarding donations mentioned first time in post-resumption pleadings (or second preliminary briefs) inadmissible as untimely even when subsequent judgment established non-loan character; timeliness required when defendant could have contested as donations in initial brief. Estate debts limited to documented amounts actually paid or invoiced; undetermined legal fee expenditures without invoices/proposals excluded. Donation between spouses regarding half-ownership property computed at one-half full ownership for donor spouse's succession. Case remanded for expert valuation of estate (relictum minus debts) and ascertained indirect donations (donatum) calculating legitimate portions and available portion per Art. 556.
